notes:
## New features
- Full CRTN 1988 for roads. Road traffic is now calculated with the complete Calculation of Road Traffic Noise procedure: emission and propagation, with finite segments, ground cover, terrain and building screening, barriers, the angle of view, opposite-facade reflections and the low-flow correction. The CRTN-emission / ISO 9613-2 propagation route remains available in Global Settings > Roads, or per road.
- Cuttings and embankments. Raising or lowering a road that is not a bridge now builds an embankment or cutting in the ground, with sloped (1:2 by default) or vertical sides. It screens in both CRTN and ISO calculations and shows in 3D.
- Roundabouts. With the Road tool, hold Shift or Option and drag from the centre to draw a roundabout; the number of segments follows its size (at least an octagon).
- Hard shoulders. Motorways show 3.3 m hard shoulders in 2D and 3D; dual carriageways can show them too (Road inspector > Hard shoulders).
- Road furniture in 3D. Motorways show a concrete step barrier and dual carriageways a steel safety barrier; road source lines can be shown as pipes at the source height.
- Global Settings rebuilt. Settings pages lay out in two columns with compact fields, point-symbol settings side by side, a new 3D view page and a Roads (CRTN) section. Controls that no longer do anything have been removed.
- New sliders and toggles across AURIS. Sliders have a soft teal track and a weighted feel, and you can double-click one to type a value. Toggles are more compact, with the same look.
- Sheet colours. One colour sets every line in the sheet side panel, and one sets the map frame, co-ordinate ticks and neatline labels.

## Changes
- Contours: Calculate keeps your chosen method (SmartSmooth, Interpolated, Scalar Field or Gradient) instead of switching to Raw. The smooth methods run the report-quality calculation, which finds building and barrier shadow edges so smooth contours no longer show stair steps along them.
- Contour calculations are much faster where buildings cast shadows: screening edges are now checked across all processor cores (identical results; one six-source, 66-building scene went from about 50 minutes to about 17), and contour meshes and SmartSmooth presentation are built several times faster.
- Older projects open with their roads converted to the new road tool, with the geometry and traffic kept. A two-way total on a dual carriageway is split evenly between directions, noted in the migration report. Roads defined by a measured level or sound power stay on the ISO route, and no longer stop the project's other roads from calculating. The old project-wide "unified ISO" transport setting is replaced by per-source routing.
- The contour sheet scale bar is thinner, and its metre labels are larger; neatline labels are larger, in regular weight, with shorter ticks.
- The contour geometry controls are two full-width sliders: Simplification, and Curve smoothing (fully left is off).
- The Update Grid bar is slimmer, with matching Update and Cancel buttons.
- The contour side panel is always shown; the hide and restore buttons have been removed.
- The 3D view opens faster: camera collision is prepared in the background and receptor symbols are built from a shared template.
- Progress bars use a subtle blue-teal gradient.

## Bug fixes
- Custom colours for the lowest and highest contour classes (below-minimum and above-maximum) were lost when a project was saved and reopened.
- The report-quality contour calculation could fail on large scenes when a small region between a screening edge and a building had no calculation points; that region is now left blank.
- A contour sheet's second basemap (layer B) was cleared when the Contours tab opened, and opening the tab marked the project as changed.
